before: parse::<u32> checks whether text is a representable unsigned integer. It does not know whether a study session should permit zero or a very large duration. trim deliberately accepts leading and trailing whitespace; that normalization is part of the chosen policy.

The helper returns a descriptive Result after enforcing 1 through 60. This sample uses static string error messages, so no owned error allocation is needed. The success branch receives only a validated minute count; parse failure and range failure remain distinguishable.
Expected output or behavior: 15. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Compare whitespace, negative text and exact boundaries; state which behavior is intentional. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

First the function removes extra spaces and reads a number. Then it checks that the number is from 1 through 60.
The output is `15`. The spaces around 15 do not change its value, and 15 fits the rule.
Try 61. Identify which check accepts it and which rejects it.
